kevin: Quick heads-up — HF->Redwood conversion surfaced strange token splits in chat-mode. Repro on a small prompt: role tokens glued to text when we run with nfkc normalization. Anyone seen this? :thinking:

anya: Can you paste a minimal repro? Is this only with chat templates or also plain generate?

kevin: Plain generate seems fine. Chat wrapper (system + user) triggers it. Here's a tiny repro (HF tokenizer vs converted):

kevin: ```py
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
# HF tokenizer loaded from repo
hf = Tokenizer.from_file('hf-tokenizer.json')
conv = Tokenizer.from_file('redwood-converted.json')
print(hf.encode('⁠ System: Hello
User: hi').tokens)
print(conv.encode('⁠ System: Hello
User: hi').tokens)
```

kevin: Output shows hf -> ['▁System', ':', '▁Hello', '
', '▁User', ':', '▁hi']
kevin: conv -> ['System', ':', '▁Hello', '
', 'User', ':', '▁hi']

marta: Oof — losing the leading underscore (add_prefix_space behavior) will change tokenization alignment and can shift attention for role tokens. Could be pre-tokenizer settings or normalizer stripping U+2060 (WORD JOINER).

anya: Which fields in config.json did the convert step map? Sometimes we lose "add_prefix_space": true for ByteLevelBPET conversions. Also check normalizer name (nfkc vs nfc) and 'byte_fallback' flag.

kevin: conv config snippet I see: { "normalizer": {"name":"nfkc"}, "pre_tokenizer": {"name":"whitespace"}, "add_prefix_space": false }

kevin: HF original had: { "normalizer": {"name":"nfkc"}, "pre_tokenizer": {"name":"byte_level"}, "add_prefix_space": true }

modelops-bot: Created conversion-job/1748 to re-run with preserved add_prefix_space + byte_level pre-tokenizer — https://redwood/jobs/1748 :eyes:

marta: Also check special tokens mapping. If our chat template relies on <|system|> or role markers that are split differently, evals will show regressions. I saw a 5% drop on the role-sensitivity test when leading spaces are removed.

anya: Good catch. Quick triage checklist: 
- re-run conversion with add_prefix_space=true
- force pre_tokenizer to byte-level/byte_fallback = true
- ensure normalizer preserves U+2060 (don't strip nonspacing joiners)
- run small eval suite (role-preservation, few-shot formatting)

kevin: I ran a local hack: patched converted tokenizer json to set "add_prefix_space": true and switched pre_tokenizer to byte-level. Reran unit tests — chat formatting regained correct tokens. Quick diff:

kevin: ```diff
- "pre_tokenizer": { "name": "whitespace" }
+ "pre_tokenizer": { "name": "byte_level", "use_regex": false }
- "add_prefix_space": false
+ "add_prefix_space": true
```

marta: Can we standardize a conversion rule: if original hf config has add_prefix_space or byte-level, preserve them. Also keep an allowlist for normalizer that doesn't remove WORD JOINER / ZERO WIDTH JOINER used in some chat templates.

anya: Agreed. Also flag for quantization runs: tokenization mismatch can amplify apparent quality regressions after int8. We should re-run quant tests after conversion fix.

modelops-bot: Scheduled eval-run/521 (regression-checker) triggered after conversion-job/1748 completes.

kevin: Next steps for me: open a PR with stricter conversion rules + unit repro and add a regression test to the onboarding pipeline that compares token lists for a small set of chat templates.

marta: I'll add a commit to the eval harness with role-preservation testcases.

anya: Thanks — please paste job ids & PR links here when ready. :thumbsup:
